title: A two-joint skin at its REST pose -- the animation arm is withheld and board:1375 says why

criterion.says: A simple example of vertex skinning in glTF

acceptanceClass.because: The framing rule's own direction over a single static body. What this decides is the skin's BIND state: joints, inverse bind matrices and the JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0 attributes all have to resolve to the same surface both sides draw before any pose can be compared.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

subjects.name: SimpleSkin
subjects.notes: Attributes JOINTS_0, POSITION, WEIGHTS_0. The file carries 1 animation over 5.5 s targeting node 2, which is a JOINT of skin 0 and therefore a BONE inside Blender's armature rather than an object -- the preparer keys animated channels by object name, so the animated arm cannot be scored yet and is withheld under board:1375 rather than declared and left refusing. THE REST POSE IS NOT A LESSER CASE: it is where the bind matrices are wrong or right.

source.pinReason: the corpus-wide pin every manifest in this tree already cites

camera.derivation: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h, quoted so the runner can refuse a mismatch rather than trust it. World bounds [-0.5, 0.0, 0.0] to [0.5, 2.0, 0.0], so centre = [0.0, 1.0, 0.0] and radius = 1.118033988749895 m. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from a 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. distance = radius / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 = 7.984601306558229, and the eye is centre + (cos20*cos35, sin20, cos20*sin35) * distance. clipStart is distance - radius and clipEnd is distance + radius.
camera.note: The glTF carries no camera, so the framing rule supplies one. Roll is 0 because the rule sets it: a roll chosen here and nowhere else would make this subject's placement a second determination competing with the rule.

light.note: The material emits, so nothing has to arrive for the picture to exist.

world.note: Declared and zero rather than left factory, so the picture is a function of this manifest and not of a Blender default.

material.note: Emission, one colour per glTF material, keyed by the name the FILE gives it. A material a primitive does not name is keyed by `<default>`, which is the format's own word for the material an undefined `material` selects.

default.note: The binary mask and the emitted colour in one render. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. A still costs one frame, so the full 1280x720 is affordable here where an animated case has to buy its grid.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe with the sampler's seed moved. At one sample per pixel of a deterministic emission there is nothing for a seed to change, so any pixel that moves between these two renders is the oracle's own noise rather than a disagreement with us -- which is what makes this the instrument floor instead of an assumption about it.

notes: A coverage case. Its shading -- textures, metallic-roughness, any extension it declares -- is NOT what this decides; board:1363 records why no case takes the shading arm yet. The animation is present in the file and DELIBERATELY not declared here; a later item takes it once a channel can be keyed to a bone.

subjectFrameFraction.note: The fraction of the frame the subject's projected area covers at frame 0. RECOMPUTED BY THE RUNNER ON EVERY RUN and refused on mismatch, so what this line does is pin it. It is seeded from that recomputation, which makes it a DRIFT DETECTOR rather than a present-error check -- honest only because the camera is independently proven to be the framing rule's.
